dissent: The docstring already disclaims digest recomputation and payload re-derivation as limitations; this review still rates them defects because 'supported' would certify unanchored bytes — a maintainer could instead read 'supported' as mere retained-field consistency, making these scope notes.

'reader-install-corrupt' unconditionally predicts 'copy-mismatch' (~L136-137); that is safe only if every fixture raw contains 'ownerA'. p_literal bytes are absent from the packet, so a no-op replace yielding 'ok' cannot be ruled out — which would flip this into a false-counterexample defect.
findings: Suffix-order control has wrong polarity (false counterexample). proposals/o22-reader-lineage-implement.py ~L344-349 (positions collected ~L311, slot-blind per-verb) emits a 'counterexample' finding whenever all six SUFFIX_ORDER verbs occur out of canonical index order. Legitimate profiles violate this: s_domain.py add('copy-not-wait', …) ~L104 orders release:0 before wait:0 then repeats release; q_domain.py add('existing-reader-new-selection', …) ~L97 interleaves request:1/pin:1 among slot-0 verbs. On full-domain retained cases a valid certificate is misclassified. Minimal fix: bind the check to the fixed-suffix (start 19) profile shape, or downgrade to an observation.

Certificate trust is unanchored. _restore (~L70-93) only relinks adjacent before/after sha256 strings; it never recomputes state digests, done-mask, requires-order, or the adapter core-done/invocation mask enforced by adapter_traces.py restore() ~L64-79. _env_pair (~L232-241) omits the signed() HMAC/payload validation and token() generation shape required by semantic.py pair_envelope ~L24-61, and inspect_cases ~L269 consumes case['incarnation_pairs'] with no schema/causal validation. Fixture: a case with self-consistent fabricated hash strings, arbitrary patched reader fields, and a forged pair row {'source':gs,'target':gt} is audited as genuine and can reach 'supported'. Minimal fix: recompute digests (requires hashlib; conflicts with the no-imports design, else verdict must be 'unproved') and validate pair rows against token() shape and causal indices before _pair uses them.

reader-install premise is weaker than the frozen guard. _expected (~L133-140) predicts 'ok' iff env.generation ∈ store-generations ∪ retired_cuts; the real guard requires raw==canonical fixture text AND env.content==fixture digest AND env.inventory==record hashes (q_audit.py 'reader-' install clause ~L117-126; q_inclusive.py equivalent). _lineage (~L207-215) checks only envelope membership and type(row[1]) is str. Fixture: reader_copies[0]=(E,'tampered-raw') with E a genuine store envelope and recorded decision 'reader-install:0:ok' — checker agrees, real guard answers 'copy-mismatch', forged certificate certified. Minimal fix: track exact copied (env,raw) rows, not generations, and require install rows to equal a previously store-validated row; absent that, 'unproved'.

Row discrimination is silently skippable and restore can crash uncharged. case.get('rows') or () (~L269) plus `if rows:` guards (~L335) mean a case lacking 'rows' evades every q_invoked/responses_related check yet may still return 'supported' (only wrong-length rows gap, ~L279). _restore (~L73) raises uncaught KeyError on an intact-passing case missing 'initial', and both full restores (~L281-282) run before the first charge.take (~L291), so precharge does not bound restore work. Minimal fix: require rows presence+length as hard schema and wrap per-case restore in the existing gap catch.
